The saved-copy feature works, including the PDF and Internet Archive paths. Ready at:

**http://maker:4001** — *(reminder: the capture is simulated here since this offline prototype can't fetch live pages; the states and actions are real, and in the finished app the actual page/PDF content is stored)*

Please try this:

1. **Save a page copy:** save the **nasa.gov** example, tap **Edit.** Under a new **"Offline copy"** section, tap **"Save a copy of this page."** The card now shows a **💾 Saved copy** badge with a **View** link — open it to see the stand-in saved page (with a banner explaining it stays readable even if the original changes or vanishes). In the editor you can also **Update copy** or **Remove copy**.

2. **Internet Archive:** in the same section tap **"Also preserve via Internet Archive."** You get a link to the web.archive.org capture, shown on the card too.

3. **A PDF:** save the **arxiv.org · a PDF** example. Its card is marked **PDF**, and in the editor the action reads **"Save the PDF file"** — saving stores the document itself, and **View** opens it as the saved PDF.

Judgement calls to confirm — including two I can only describe, since they involve live fetching this offline prototype can't do:

- I made saving a copy a **per-bookmark choice** (you decide which links are worth keeping offline), rather than automatically copying every page. Right call, or would you want it automatic on save?
- The **local saved copy** and the **Internet Archive** copy are **two separate options** — one stored by your app, one preserved publicly on archive.org. Does having both, independently, match what you wanted?
- In the real app, if the **original page later changes or disappears**, your saved copy and the archive link **still open** the captured version. And if a capture **fails** (site unreachable), I'd keep the bookmark and tell you the copy couldn't be made, so you can retry. Do those behaviours match your intent?

Does the saved-copy feature behave the way you had in mind?
